title: Effect of yogurt consumption on periodontal inflammation in patients with periodontitis- a randomized controlled trial
summary:
The planned study will investigate the influence of an anti-inflammatory, probiotic diet on gum inflammation in periodontitis patients. The research question is whether 60 days of yoghurt consumption reduces gum inflammation compared to patients without yoghurt consumption. Therefore, a prospective, controlled, randomized, single-blind (investigator) clinical trial with two groups (test and control) will be conducted. 
Adults ≥18 years of age with generalized periodontitis who have at least 10 teeth and 40% inflamed areas on the gums will be recruited. Patients with severe general diseases (e.g. infections, malignant tumors), with medication that changes the inflammatory behavior of the gums, patients who already have a high consumption of natural yogurt, smoke more than 10 cigarettes a day, have planned major dental treatments, are lactose intolerant, pregnant or breastfeeding will not be included in the study.
Initially, the subjects are informed about the study and checked for suitability for participation. Written patient information is handed out and consent is obtained later on.
This is followed by the baseline examination (visit 1). Patients receive a nutrition questionnaire. A dental examination of the oral cavity is performed and all study parameters (clinical attachment loss, probing depths, probing blood levels, etc.) are recorded.
Assignment to the respective group (yogurt group / non-yogurt group) is randomized. The patients in the test group receive the yoghurt for the first 7 days and eat 150 g twice a day. The yoghurt consumption is documented in a protocol. Further portions of yoghurt are handed out every week. During the study, all subjects maintain their usual diet and oral hygiene.
The final examination (visit 2) takes place after 60 +/- 3 days. At this appointment, the same parameters are recorded, adverse effects are recorded and professional tooth cleaning is carried out on all test subjects.
The hypothesis of the study is that the inflammation values on the gums (bleeding) will decrease in the test group, while there will be no change in the control group.

interventions.name: Test group: yoghurt consumption 2 x 150 g per day for 60 days
Control group: no additional yogurt consumption over 60 days

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adults ≥18 years of age
- Generalized periodontitis stage 3 grades B-C
- At least 10 own teeth
- BOP ≥ 40 %
- Signed informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Severe general diseases (e.g. infections, malignant tumors)
- Antibiotics taken 6 weeks before the start of the study
- Taking medication that can change the bleeding or inflammatory behavior of the gums (e.g. anticoagulants, steroids, NSAIR)
- Pregnancy, breastfeeding
- Women of childbearing potential without contraception
- Lactose intolerance
- Already high consumption of natural yoghurt
- Unwillingness to abstain from yoghurt consumption during the study with the exception of the yoghurt consumption specified by the study
- Smoking > 10 cig/day (equivalent to other tobacco products)
- Planned dental treatments (e.g. prophylaxis, periodontitis treatment, prosthetic restorations)
- Simultaneous participation in other clinical trials (up to 4 weeks before the start of the study)
